sources.title: Nesta van der Schaaf, Classical and Quantum Particles in Galilean and Poincaré Spacetime (2017)
sources.locator: Complete 85-page monograph PDF inspected. §9.3, PDF pp. 77–79; §10.2.2, PDF pp. 81–82. Source uses natural units and signature (+---); the authored statements translate to SI and (-+++).

contents.name: Proper orthochronous Poincaré massive coadjoint-orbit classification, §9.3, PDF pp. 77–79
contents.support: The full classification passage was inspected; the local proof recomputes the exact stabilizers, dimensions, and W invariant with the repository metric and units.

contents.name: Massive spinless and positive classical-spin orbit branches, §9.3, PDF pp. 77–79
contents.support: The source cross-checks the six-dimensional spinless and eight-dimensional nonzero-spin branches; the local proof supplies the explicit global shell coordinates and KKS form identification.

contents.name: Classical continuous-spin discussion versus quantum spin interpretation, §10.2.2, PDF pp. 81–82
contents.support: This passage is used only to delimit the optional classical model: the postulate explicitly makes no quantum-spectrum or Wigner-representation claim and does not infer a physical model from the orbit.

alternatives.argument: The item proves local existence directly: the smooth-dependence theorem supplies Hamilton characteristics, the choice-free inverse theorem supplies the actual invertible projection domain, and differentiating the endpoint action with integration by parts yields S_q=p and S_t=-H. This is a complete local proof before caustics and does not rely on the MIT notes.

The item differentiates the HJ equation to prove beta=S_alpha is constant, computes dq wedge dp=d beta wedge d alpha from the symmetric mixed Hessian, and derives the covariant-to-time HJ equation from the future shell root. These complete local calculations do not rely on the MIT notes.

sources.title: Andrew Hanson, Tullio Regge and Claudio Teitelboim, Constrained Hamiltonian Systems, Part 1 (1976)
sources.locator: 35-page Part 1 PDF inspected. Chapter I, printed pp. 7–11; the weak-equality and first-class criterion is at printed pp. 9–10.

contents.name: Weak equality and first-class constraint criterion, Chapter I pp. 9–10
contents.support: Henneaux, Regge and Teitelboim define first-class quantities by weak Poisson commutation with every constraint. Applied to the constraints themselves, this gives pairwise bracket vanishing on the regular common surface, the exact local convention defined here.

contents.name: Constraint tangency and multiplier consistency, Chapter I pp. 8–10
contents.support: The discussion derives tangency from weak preservation and distinguishes multiplier conditions from additional constraints; the assigned example computes its own regular on-surface witness.

sources.title: Ghanashyam Date, Lectures on Constrained Systems, arXiv:1010.2062 (2010)
sources.locator: 28-page PDF inspected. §3, PDF pp. 13–14, Eq. (3.9), and §4, PDF p. 20, Eq. (4.22), on weak equality, consistency and first-class bracket closure.

contents.name: Weak equality and first-class constraint bracket closure, §4 Eq. (4.22), PDF p. 20
contents.support: Date gives the weakly vanishing pairwise brackets as the first-class condition for constraints and relates weak closure to coefficients multiplying constraints. The local definition uses the weaker pointwise-on-N statement and makes no coefficient-regularity claim.

contents.name: Multiplier tangency and consistency equation, §3 Eq. (3.9), PDF pp. 13–14
contents.support: Date derives the weak tangency equation and explains that a nonzero constraint-bracket matrix constrains multipliers; the example independently computes its bracket and explicit joint-surface witness.
